title: Fix the Shared Default List
description: The program should add an item to a fresh shopping list each time the function is called without an explicit list. Fix the bug.
buggyCode:
def add_item(item, cart=[]):
    cart.append(item)
    return cart

print(add_item("apple"))
print(add_item("banana"))
expectedBehavior: Each call without an explicit cart should start from an empty list, so the program should print ['apple'] then ['banana'].
actualProblem: Default argument values are created once, when the function is defined, and reused across all calls. Since cart=[] is mutable, every call that doesn't pass its own list keeps appending to the very same list, so the second call prints ['apple', 'banana'] instead of a fresh ['banana'].
correctedCode:
def add_item(item, cart=None):
    if cart is None:
        cart = []
    cart.append(item)
    return cart

print(add_item("apple"))
print(add_item("banana"))
explanation: To avoid the shared mutable default trap, use None as the default and create a brand new list inside the function body each time one isn't provided. This guarantees every call starts fresh.
